target_customer: Oncology patients and pharma partners; revenue expected from drug development and partnerships (a research collaboration with Johnson & Johnson Enterprise Innovation is reported)
problem: Systemic cancer drugs reach healthy tissue and cause toxicity; delivering and activating drugs only at the tumor could widen the therapeutic window.
business_model: Clinical-stage biotech developing proprietary therapeutics and licensing or partnering platform assets
product_category: Oncology therapeutics using click chemistry (CAPAC platform)

founders.name: Jose M. Mejia Oneto
previous_startups: Tambo (earlier YC company that spun off Shasqi in 2018, per the YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page describes him as a physician-scientist with clinical training in orthopedics. A search result says he was an orthopedic surgery resident who began researching click and bioorthogonal chemistry in 2014.

technical_complexity.rationale: Using bioorthogonal click chemistry inside the human body to activate drugs at tumors had no precedent and required novel chemistry, biomaterials and clinical translation.

defensibility.rationale: Proprietary CAPAC platform with first-in-human click chemistry data and clinical development barriers; intellectual property details were not opened.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent was found copying the approach; a research collaboration with Johnson & Johnson Enterprise Innovation was reported in 2022 and strengthened in 2023.

market_need_then: Chemotherapy toxicity and the need for tumor-selective delivery were well known; click chemistry and bioorthogonal chemistry were later recognised by the 2022 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

identity.logo: Brandfetch lists logo files but gives no description
identity.voice_and_tone: Scientific; mission to revolutionize cancer treatment with click chemistry

branding.community_and_virality: Trade press on the first click chemistry use in humans (The Scientist, Endpoints, PharmaVoice per search results), mostly about the science rather than the brand.

brand_strength.rationale: An invented name with no sourced story and recognition mainly among biotech readers.

outcome_analysis: Shasqi raised a $10M Series A in October 2019 and a $50M Series B in November 2021, brought its lead click chemistry protodrug into first-in-human trials and secured NIH grants and a J&J research collaboration, and remains active with about 28 staff. Its path rests on a hard technical platform with clinical validation, though final outcomes depend on later trials.
notes: The Series B of $50M (announced 2021-11-11) comes from a Fierce Biotech headline and a BusinessWire release URL dated 20211111; both returned 403 on fetch so investors and lead are unknown. BioSpace says Shasqi was founded in 2018 while YC lists 2015 and the YC page says Tambo spun it off in 2018; founding year 2015 kept from the YC page. Aggregators give totals of $52M to $63.5M and NCI and NIH grants (including $2M in 2021 and more than $8M since 2021); grants not recorded as rounds because amounts and dates are unverified. YC page says the company raised more than $60M. No dated competitor sources near 2015 were found. No negative outcome news found.
